title: PR2: per-session note grouping with embedded JSONL summary as title
description:
Second of two PRs improving Evernote note quality. Solves note discovery: each Claude Code session becomes its own Evernote note with the title derived from Claude Code's auto-generated summary message embedded in the JSONL.

Key insight (via daaain/claude-code-log): Claude Code already writes summary messages into JSONL files (type='summary', with fields summary and leafUuid). leafUuid points to a message UUID, used to match summary to session. Cross-session matching is needed because Claude Code can write a summary for session A into session B's file (Issue #2597). No LLM call required.

Implementation steps:

1. parser.py — recognize type='summary' records during parsing; expose them alongside Sessions for cross-file matching.
2. New cross-session matching pass: collect all summaries from all parsed files; build leafUuid -> session_id map from messages; attach summary to the right Session.
3. Session dataclass — add optional 'summary' field.
4. grouping.py — replace {(date, repo): [Session,...]} buckets with per-session shape; long-running sessions are no longer fragmented across daily notes.
5. state.py — track per-session: {session_id: {synced_uuids, finalized, last_activity}}; idle threshold = 24h since last message (configurable).
6. email destination — note title becomes <summary or first-prompt fallback>; updates append while session is active, finalize after idle.
7. api destination — per-session upsert keyed on session_id.
8. main.py — wire it all together.

Note title format: if summary exists, use it; otherwise fall back to first user prompt (truncated). Include repo + short session id as suffix so similar-titled notes can be disambiguated.

Should land after claude-evernote-sync-bfa (PR1). Beads dep: claude-evernote-sync-bfa.
notes: Closed by PR #10 (merged 2026-05-20) — embedded-summary parser + cross-file matching + in-note session headers. The remaining per-session restructure is tracked separately in claude-evernote-sync-47c.

title: PR1: rendering cleanup (strip ANSI, filter slash-command lifecycle, render markdown)
description:
First of two PRs improving Evernote note quality. Three concrete rendering bugs observed in example output:

1. ANSI escape codes leak through (e.g. '[1mOpus 4.7[22m' visible in rendered notes) — ESC was stripped upstream but SGR brackets remain
2. Slash command lifecycle messages render as 3-4 separate User messages (<local-command-caveat>, <command-name>, <command-args>, <local-command-stdout>) — should be filtered out entirely
3. Markdown is not converted to ENML — **bold**, ## headings, [link](url), inline code show as literal characters

Approach (per discussion with user, TDD red-green):
- parser.py: filter slash-command lifecycle messages + strip ANSI sequences from extracted message text (clean text in Session.messages — destination-agnostic)
- formatter.py: convert markdown to ENML at render time (destination-specific; the API destination's ENML and the email HTML both benefit)
- Survey daaain/claude-code-log for reusable rendering bits (MIT, Python, same JSONL input format)

Keeps coverage >= 80%, file <= 200 lines, function <= 20 lines, params <= 3, nesting <= 2.
notes: Closed by PR #9 (merged 2026-05-20). Strip-ANSI, slash-command filter, markdown→ENML rendering are all live on main.

title: strip_code_fences mangles multi/nested-fence messages (orphan lang tags, lost indentation)
description: parser.py strip_code_fences uses a non-greedy regex over triple-backtick fences that mis-pairs them when a message has multiple or nested fences. Real example: a user prompt with 8 fences (a pasted thread whose body is itself fenced, with python code nested inside). Rendered result: an orphaned bare python language line, raw un-monospaced code with lost indentation, and leaked ### markdown. Fix: stop regex-stripping; render fenced code via the markdown fenced_code extension as pre (monospace survives Evernote per the probe; codehilite does NOT, inner spans are stripped). This is the code half of content_depth (-qxy) and can be fixed as part of it or standalone first.
acceptance_criteria: Messages with multiple or nested fences render cleanly; fenced code shows as pre monospace with preserved indentation; no orphaned language tags leak into the note.

title: content_depth config: surface tool calls + code under foldable headings
description: Parser (parser.py:89) keeps only type==text blocks, dropping all tool_use/tool_result/thinking and stripping fenced code. A real session surfaced ~20 of ~85 content blocks. Add config [render].content_depth = full|tools|conversation (default full). full: render tool calls as compact monospace lines under a foldable Tool activity heading + restore fenced code as pre. tools: tool lines, no code. conversation: status quo. Heading-based collapsibility confirmed working via email.
acceptance_criteria: content_depth validated; tool calls rendered compactly under foldable headings; code restored in full; conversation mode equals current behavior; default full.

title: Sub-agent transcripts: clean titles from meta.json + subagent_notes config
description: discover_jsonl_files (main.py:38) uses rglob, sweeping in Claude Code sub-agent transcripts under <session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl. These carry the PARENT sessionId so attach_ai_titles never matches them, and the title falls back to the verbose parent task prompt (READ-ONLY audit...). Each has a sibling agent-*.meta.json with a clean agentType+description. Add config [render].subagent_notes = keep|suppress (default keep). keep: title sub-agent notes from the meta.json description; suppress: exclude subagents/ from discovery. merge mode deferred.
acceptance_criteria: subagent_notes config validated; default keep titles sub-agent notes from meta.json description; suppress excludes them from discovery; top-level session titles unaffected.

title: Beautify rendered notes: drop duplicate title, role labels, survivor-only styling
description: Body repeats the note title as an h1 (formatter.py:120); bland User/Assistant labels with second-precision timestamps; cramped italic metadata line. Empirical probe through the real email-to-ENML path showed typography survives (color, font-size, weight, monospace, h1-h3 headings that FOLD in-app, lists, tables, code, pre) but ALL box styling (background, border, padding, margin, hr), en-todo, and astral emoji are stripped. This PR: drop the redundant h1; colored+bold You/Claude role labels; minute-precision timestamps in small-gray; small-gray metadata line. No parser changes.
acceptance_criteria: No h1 duplicating the note title; user turns labeled You and assistant Claude, colored+bold; per-message timestamps are HH:MM with no seconds; only survivor styling primitives used; tests and coverage pass.
notes: Validated on real content via preview_render (PDF en_recent_3_notes): colored You/Claude, no duplicate h1, small-gray metadata, minute timestamps, foldable assistant headings all confirmed. Awaiting merge of PR #16.

title: PR3 (deferred): per-session Evernote notes (one note per session, summary as title)
description:
Deferred from claude-evernote-sync-cer. The summary parsing + in-note headers (PR for feat/embedded-summaries branch) handles in-note discovery. The remaining piece is restructuring grouping/state/destinations so each Claude Code session becomes its own Evernote note with the summary as the note title in Evernote's list view.

Scope:
- grouping.py — replace GroupKey=(date_iso, bucket) with per-session key; long-running sessions are no longer fragmented across daily notes.
- state.py — per-session tracking model: {session_id: {synced_uuids, finalized: bool, last_activity: datetime, locked_title: str}}. Bump STATE_VERSION (existing state file discarded).
- main.py — pass per-session SyncContext; sync logic remains idempotent.
- destinations/email.py — note subject = locked title (summary or first-prompt fallback); append-while-active, no more sends after finalization.
- destinations/api.py — per-session upsert keyed on session_id.
- formatter.note_title — new format using summary; lock the title at first sync (later summary records DON'T retitle the existing note because email subject is the unique key).
- Idle threshold = 24h since last message (configurable). Once idle, session is finalized; new messages after that are treated as a continuation of a 'new' session for archival purposes.

User-impact / migration:
- Existing daily-rollup notes in Evernote stay as-is (not migrated).
- After this lands, the lookback window will re-sync sessions as per-session notes — duplicates with the prior daily-rollups for that window. User would need to delete duplicates manually or accept the overlap.
- Recommend documenting the migration in README and the PR description.

Title format proposal:
- With summary:    '<summary> · <bucket>'
- Without summary: '<first 60 chars of first user prompt> · <bucket>'

Optional follow-up: rip claude-code-log's ai-title support too (separate JSONL record type with type='ai-title').
notes: Starting work — list-view discovery confirmed as the remaining pain after #10. Per-session notes with summary-as-title is the right next step.

title: Optional LLM bullet-summary block (claude -p)
description:
Deferred from initial discovery-and-rendering work. After per-session note grouping (PR2) lands with embedded JSONL summaries used as titles, evaluate whether the title alone solves note discovery. If we still want a richer summary block at the top of each note, implement an optional 'Tier 2' step:

- Shell out to claude -p '<prompt>' --output-format json on each session at finalization time
- Returns 3-5 bullet summary; embedded at top of the note's ENML body
- Off by default in config; user opts in
- Truncate session to bounded input window (first prompt + last N messages + files touched) so per-call cost stays in the cents-per-month range
- Cache the summary in state so we only call once per session
- Fall back to deterministic header on failure (CLI missing, bucket exhausted, network error)

Cost/billing context (as of 2026):
- Before June 15, 2026: claude -p draws from interactive subscription
- After June 15, 2026: draws from a separate monthly Agent SDK credit (Pro , Max5x , Max20x/Enterprise-Premium-seat ; Enterprise Standard seats NOT eligible)
- Architecture must degrade gracefully when no credit is available

Do not implement until PR1 (rendering cleanup) and PR2 (per-session notes with embedded summary titles) have shipped and Tier 1 has been evaluated in real use.
